memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Chronic plaque psoriasis, benign positional vertigo, and polycystic ovary syndrome.
Symptoms and examination: She reports scaly erythematous plaques on elbows and knees, intermittent spinning sensation on lying down, and irregular menstrual cycles with hirsutism. Examination shows well-demarcated silvery-scaled plaques over extensor surfaces, positive Dix-Hallpike on right side, and bilateral ovarian enlargement on palpation.
Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream apply BD to affected areas
calcipotriol ointment apply OD to plaques
methotrexate 7.5 mg oral once weekly
folic acid 5 mg oral daily
metformin 500 mg oral BD
combined oral contraceptive pill (ethinylestradiol 30 mcg + levonorgestrel 150 mcg) OD

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Chronic plaque psoriasis, benign positional vertigo, polycystic ovary syndrome (stable).
Symptoms and examination: Plaques show mild thinning and less scaling; vertigo episodes now once weekly, less severe; menstrual cycles more regular with reduced hirsutism. Examination: faint pink patches on elbows, no active scaling; Dix-Hallpike negative bilaterally; ovaries not enlarged on palpation.
Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
methotrexate 10 mg oral once weekly (increased from 7.5 mg)
folic acid 5 mg oral daily
all other medications unchanged

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dix-Hallpike test: Positive on right side with transient torsional nystagmus lasting <1 minute, consistent with benign positional vertigo. Left side negative.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been taking meclizine 25 mg when I feel dizzy and it helps; the spinning attacks are now rare and mild.

memories.author: D05

Diagnosis: Chronic plaque psoriasis, benign positional vertigo, polycystic ovary syndrome (mild liver enzyme rise).
Symptoms and examination: Plaques unchanged; vertigo infrequent; menstrual regularity maintained. Mild transaminitis noted on labs.
Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
methotrexate 7.5 mg oral once weekly (reduced from 10 mg due to ALT/AST rise)
folic acid 5 mg oral daily
all other medications unchanged

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Chronic plaque psoriasis, benign positional vertigo, polycystic ovary syndrome (liver enzymes improving).
Symptoms and examination: Plaques show slight improvement; vertigo absent for past 3 weeks; menstrual cycles regular, no hirsutism progression.
Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream BD to plaques
calcipotriol ointment OD to plaques (continued)
methotrexate 7.5 mg oral once weekly
folic acid 5 mg oral daily
metformin 500 mg oral BD
combined oral contraceptive pill OD

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Pelvic ultrasound: Bilateral ovaries show multiple small follicles (6‑9 mm) with increased stromal echogenicity; uterine lining normal. Consistent with polycystic ovarian morphology.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum testosterone 49 ng/dL (15-70).
LH 5.8 mIU/mL (2-12); FSH 5.5 mIU/mL (2-10); LH:FSH ratio 1.05.
HbA1c 5.3% (4.0-5.6).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Chronic plaque psoriasis, benign positional vertigo, polycystic ovary syndrome (well controlled).
Symptoms and examination: Plaques flat, minimal scaling; no vertigo episodes in past 2 months; menstrual cycles regular, no acne/hirsutism worsening.
Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0.

folic acid 5 mg oral daily continued
clobetasol 0.05% cream BD to plaques
calcipotriol ointment OD to plaques
